name: USearch
tagline: Single-header C++ HNSW library with SIMD distance kernels and bindings for a dozen languages.
description: USearch is a compact HNSW implementation from Unum Cloud, shipped as a single C++11 header with bindings for Python, JavaScript, Rust, Java, Go, C#, Swift, Objective-C, Wolfram and WebAssembly. It uses SimSIMD kernels for fast distance computation, supports custom metrics and f64 to binary quantization, and can serve an index directly from disk via memory-mapping. Its small footprint and permissive licence have made it the ANN engine inside other databases, including ClickHouse's vector similarity index and DuckDB's VSS extension. Use it when you are building search into software, not when you need a database.

scale.notes: Single-process index; billion-scale indexes on one machine are demonstrated, distribution is up to the host application.

strengths: Single header, tiny binary, easy to embed anywhere
SIMD-accelerated distances with f16, i8 and binary quantization
Serve indexes from disk via mmap without loading into RAM
Custom metrics, including JIT-compiled user functions
weaknesses: A library only: no metadata store, filters or durability layer
HNSW only; no IVF or DiskANN options
API surface varies slightly across language bindings
useCases: Embedding ANN search into a database or application
Fast similarity joins and clustering in data pipelines
notIdealFor: Teams wanting a ready-made vector database server
